- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent 7-day low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model overreacts to sentiment shifts — smooth transitions by averaging 2–3 prior values before forecasting.
